answer: In our network, game-theoretic multi-agent auditing enforces topological cut verifications across transaction paths. When an adversarial cluster attempts coordination, random auditor committees inspect the graph structure; any forged partition acts like an ember igniting immediate stake slashing. To bypass this, an attacker must crack the committee quorum like a walnut, requiring superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size. A Sybil assault rapidly burns through collateral like a fallen comet, rendering coordinated subversion economically unviable.
